config.title: Design Permission System

intro.title: Design Permission System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple permission system for a React app that controls which users can view or edit content. You will learn how to use TypeScript to define user roles and permissions as structured types, ensuring your code is type-safe and clear. The core concepts involve creating reusable React components that conditionally render UI elements based on a user's permissions. By the end, you will have a functional system that displays or hides buttons and sections depending on whether a user is an 'admin', 'editor', or 'viewer'.
intro.usecase: Permission systems are foundational to enterprise applications like admin dashboards, SaaS platforms, and internal tools, where different user roles (e.g., admin, editor, viewer) need access to specific features. For example, in a content management system, an admin might see buttons to delete users or modify settings, while an editor only sees options to create and edit posts. As a developer, you'll implement such systems to conditionally render UI elements—like menus, action buttons, or entire panels—based on user permissions, ensuring security and a tailored user experience.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define user permission roles and actions
Construct a React component that conditionally renders UI elements based on user permissions
Configure a permission context provider to manage authentication state across components
Apply permission checks to control access to specific application features
Initialize and update permission state in response to user authentication events
Integrate permission-based routing to restrict navigation to authorized pages
Manipulate UI visibility by binding component display logic to permission states

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have the necessary React APIs imported to build components with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define the Permission type interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Permission' with three properties: 'id' (string), 'name' (string), and 'description' (string).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define the Permission interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Permission interface is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The Permission interface has id, name, and description properties with string types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all three properties (id, name, description) are defined with string types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three properties with string types.

steps.title: Create the PermissionSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named PermissionSystem that returns JSX.Element. Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that will serve as the main container for your permission system. Start with the component name and return a placeholder like null or an empty fragment for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named PermissionSystem is defined, returning JSX.Element.
successCriteria: The PermissionSystem component is defined with the correct name and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'PermissionSystem' and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check the name and return type.

steps.title: Initialize permissions state with sample data
steps.instruction: Inside the PermissionSystem component, call useState<Permission[]> with an initial array containing at least two sample permission objects.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to create state that will hold an array of Permission objects. Provide an initial array with sample data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'permissions' initialized with an array of sample permission objects.
successCriteria: useState is called with type Permission[] and an initial array containing at least two permission objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct type (Permission[]) and providing at least two sample objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState<Permission[]> with an initial array of permission objects.

steps.title: Create a function to toggle permission status
steps.instruction: Inside the PermissionSystem component, create a function named togglePermission that takes a permission id (number) as a parameter and toggles an 'enabled' boolean property on the matching permission object.
steps.hint: You'll need to update the permissions state by mapping through the array and toggling the enabled property for the permission with the matching id.
steps.expectedOutcome: The togglePermission function should be defined inside the component and properly update the permissions state when called.
successCriteria: A togglePermission function exists that takes a number parameter and updates the permissions state by toggling an 'enabled' property on the matching permission.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly updates the state using setPermissions and toggles the 'enabled' property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The togglePermission function is missing or doesn't properly update the permissions state. Check that it takes an id parameter and toggles the 'enabled' property on the matching permission.

steps.title: Add a container div to the component return
steps.instruction: In the PermissionSystem component, replace the current return statement with a div element that has a className of 'permission-system'.
steps.hint: The return statement should now render a div with the specified className attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element with className='permission-system', which will serve as the container for the permission system UI.
successCriteria: The return statement renders a div element
The div has a className attribute set to 'permission-system'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the div has exactly the className 'permission-system'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should render a div element with className='permission-system' instead of returning null.

steps.title: Add a heading to display the system title
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an h1 element with the text 'Permission System'.
steps.hint: Add the heading element directly inside the container div you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now displays a clear title 'Permission System' at the top of the interface.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Permission System' is added inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a heading, but check that it's an h1 element with exactly 'Permission System' as text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add an h1 element with 'Permission System' inside the container div.

steps.title: Map over permissions to display each one
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, below the heading, map over the permissions state to render a div for each permission, displaying its name and description.
steps.hint: Use the .map() method on the permissions array. For each permission, return a div containing its name and description.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display a list of permissions, each showing its name and description, rendered from the state array.
successCriteria: The permissions state is mapped to render a div for each permission, with the permission's name and description displayed inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the .map() method on the permissions array and returning a div for each item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The permissions are not being displayed. Check that you're mapping over the permissions state and rendering the name and description for each.

steps.title: Add a toggle button for each permission
steps.instruction: Inside each permission's div in the map function, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls togglePermission with that permission's id.
steps.hint: Add <button onClick={() => togglePermission(permission.id)}>Toggle</button> inside the div that displays each permission.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each permission item will display a 'Toggle' button that, when clicked, will call the togglePermission function with the corresponding permission id.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick handler calling togglePermission(permission.id) is added inside each permission's div in the map function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure the onClick handler correctly calls togglePermission with the permission's id. Check that you're using the right syntax: onClick={() => togglePermission(permission.id)}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle button isn't properly implemented. You need to add a button element inside each permission's div with an onClick handler that calls togglePermission(permission.id).

steps.title: Display the enabled status for each permission
steps.instruction: Inside the permission display div, add a paragraph element that shows the current enabled status of each permission.
steps.hint: Use the permission.enabled property to conditionally display 'Enabled' or 'Disabled' text.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each permission item will now show a status paragraph indicating whether it's enabled or disabled.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays 'Enabled' or 'Disabled' based on the permission.enabled property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the permission.enabled property to conditionally show the status text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status paragraph isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're using the permission.enabled property and showing appropriate text.
